article_title: Nepal bet nearly everything on hydropower - the floods show why that's a problem

tasks.prompt: What is the central argument of the article?
options: Nepal should immediately abandon all electricity exports
Nepal's hydropower success has created a climate-exposed dependence that requires stronger design, diversification and regional cooperation
Solar power caused the recent floods in the Trishuli basin
Hydropower plants face no special risks when built high in the Himalayas
tasks.correct_answer: Nepal's hydropower success has created a climate-exposed dependence that requires stronger design, diversification and regional cooperation
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הטענה המרכזית היא שההישענות הכמעט מוחלטת על הידרו־חשמל הביאה הצלחה אך גם יצרה סיכון אקלימי מערכתי שמחייב שינוי מדיניות.

tasks.prompt: What was the immediate effect of the floods on Nepal's electricity system?
options: They increased electricity exports by $200m
They destroyed every reservoir-based plant
They damaged 12 hydropower plants and removed more than 10% of total generation capacity
They caused Nepal to close all 225 plants permanently
tasks.correct_answer: They damaged 12 hydropower plants and removed more than 10% of total generation capacity
tasks.explanation_hebrew: השיטפונות פגעו קשות ב־12 תחנות באגן טרישולי והשביתו יותר מעשרה אחוזים מכושר הייצור הכולל.

tasks.prompt: Which change helped Nepal move from severe power cuts to mostly continuous electricity by 2018?
options: Hydropower expansion, anti-corruption efforts and imports from India to cover seasonal gaps
Closing mountain plants and relying entirely on coal
Ending all cross-border electricity trade
Reducing household access to electricity
tasks.correct_answer: Hydropower expansion, anti-corruption efforts and imports from India to cover seasonal gaps
tasks.explanation_hebrew: השיפור נבע מהרחבת תשתיות ההידרו, טיפול בשחיתות ויבוא חשמל מהודו להשלמת מחסור עונתי.

tasks.prompt: Why does the “all our eggs in one basket” metaphor apply to Nepal?
options: Most plants use identical baskets to carry equipment
Nearly all electricity comes from one climate-vulnerable energy source
Nepal exports electricity to only one household
All hydropower facilities belong to a single private insurer
tasks.correct_answer: Nearly all electricity comes from one climate-vulnerable energy source
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המטפורה מדגישה שכמעט כל החשמל מגיע ממקור אחד החשוף לאותם סיכוני שיטפונות, קרחונים והרים מתחממים.

tasks.prompt: What does “laid bare the risks” mean in the opening section?
options: Covered the damaged plants with mud
Made the risks clearly visible
Calculated the insurance premiums
Reduced the risks permanently
tasks.explanation_hebrew: laid bare פירושו חשף בבירור; האסון המחיש את הפגיעוּת של אסטרטגיית ההידרו־חשמל.

tasks.prompt: What does “unfeasible” mean when rising insurance costs are discussed?
options: More profitable than before
Required by international law
Impractical or financially unsustainable
Protected from all future floods
tasks.explanation_hebrew: unfeasible פירושו בלתי מעשי או לא בר־קיימא כלכלית; הפרמיות העולות מקשות על כדאיות הפעילות.

tasks.prompt: Use the article's figures to explain both the achievements and the exposure of Nepal's hydropower sector.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשתמש לפחות בחמישה נתונים מספריים מדויקים ולחברם לטיעון.
expected_points: Almost 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower
Electricity exports earn nearly $200m per year
Only two-thirds of the population had electricity access in 2010
Some connected households faced cuts of up to 16 hours a day
By 2018 most of Nepal had 24-hour supply
There are 225 plants with more than 3,900MW installed capacity
That capacity can power roughly three million households at once
Twelve plants were severely damaged in the recent floods
More than 10% of national generation capacity was knocked out
More than 1,300 people were killed and thousands remained missing

tasks.prompt: Why is switching from mountain run-of-river projects to reservoir-based plants not a complete solution?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את יתרון האגירה לצד עלויות, סיכונים ומגבלות מערכתיות.
expected_points: Reservoir plants could be placed away from some high-mountain hazards
They can store water and release it when needed
They could improve seasonal flexibility and resilience
They involve significant economic costs
They can impose major environmental costs
Changing plant type does not remove all flood and climate risks
Existing infrastructure and investments remain exposed
Diversification into wind and solar and better warning systems are still needed

tasks.prompt: Summarise why Nepal's hydropower strategy is being reconsidered and the main responses proposed in the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול הצלחות עבר, נזקי השיטפון, סיכוני אקלים, ביקורת על תכנון ומימון, ופתרונות מוצעים.
expected_points: Hydropower ended long power shortages and now supports exports
Nepal relies on it for almost all electricity
Recent floods damaged 12 plants and more than 10% of capacity
High Himalayan regions are warming faster than the global average
Past disasters show repeated vulnerability in the Trishuli basin
Critics say known risks were not adequately reflected in design and investment
Plants should be redesigned and sited for greater resilience
Early-warning and evacuation systems should be strengthened
Reservoir projects may add flexibility
Wind and solar could reduce single-source dependence
International data sharing and cooperation are needed

tasks.prompt: Write a policy briefing recommending three priorities for Nepal's electricity strategy after the floods.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית מסמך מאוזן, לבחור שלוש עדיפויות ולבסס כל אחת בעובדות מן הכתבה ובמגבלות מעשיות.
expected_points: Prioritise flood-resilient plant design and safer site selection
Install robust early-warning and emergency evacuation systems
Diversify with meaningful additions of solar and wind
Consider reservoir-based plants while acknowledging economic and environmental costs
Review lender and regulator risk assessments and enforce safeguards
Coordinate climate data and warnings with neighbouring governments and international organisations
Protect reliable supply while retaining hydropower's regional competitive advantage
Cite the loss of more than 10% of capacity or damage to 12 plants
Mention rising insurance costs and repeated Trishuli-basin floods
Avoid claiming that one technology can eliminate all climate risk
